hero.name: Fay Lyu (HazezZ)
hero.subtitle: Optimization · Formal Verification (Isabelle/HOL) · Mathematical Modeling
hero.positioning: Current work includes (i) Isabelle/HOL formalization of greedy guarantees for monotone submodular maximization, (ii) duality / lower-bound diagnostics for objectives with invariances (translation / non-identifiability), and (iii) small prototypes that turn signal-like inputs into discrete, checkable structure. This page is a quick faculty entry; see Projects for evidence/demos and CV for application-facing experience.

interests.title: Research interests (current)
items: Optimization: duality, lower bounds, first-order structure, and modeling under invariances.
Formal methods: Isabelle/HOL proof engineering (locales, interfaces, reusable lemmas).
Submodular algorithms: greedy variants, oracle interfaces, and cost-aware proof structure.
Game/strategic models as a language for structure (when useful for optimization framing).
Prototypes: signal-to-structure pipelines with explicit assumptions and failure modes.

projects_section.title: Current Projects (3 entry points)
projects_section.lead: Editorial summary cards: problem, method, contribution, status, and links. Longer technical context lives in the notes.

projects.title: An Ongoing Isabelle Research Project: Formalising Submodular Greedy
projects.problem: Machine-check the classical greedy (1−1/e) guarantee for monotone submodular maximization under a cardinality constraint.
projects.method: Build a reusable Isabelle/HOL development (locales + step-spec interfaces), separating constructive algorithm structure from approximation analysis.
projects.contribution: A proof skeleton that scales to variants (e.g., LazyGreedy/StochasticGreedy) and keeps assumptions explicit and reusable.

projects.title: Spring 2026 | Duality under Invariances (Cornell ORIE)
projects.problem: Find nontrivial lower bounds for a graph-relative-difference distance-fitting objective where natural formulations can collapse due to translation invariance / non-identifiability.
projects.method: Diagnose degeneracy first (what makes the dual trivial), then add structure (gauge-fixing / tighter constraints / augmentation) before choosing a dualization route (Fenchel/DC vs. Lagrangian).
projects.contribution: A structure-first roadmap: when/why bounds collapse, plus candidate fixes that restore informative dual signals.

projects.title: Metalcore Piano Lab | From Audio to Chart (WIP)
projects.problem: Map continuous audio (or MIDI) into a playable rhythm-game chart as a discretization problem with constraints.
projects.method: Onset/beat detection, tempo tracking, segmentation/alignment, then playability-oriented constraints and evaluation targets.
projects.contribution: A browser-native prototype + notes that document assumptions, failure modes, and next-step heuristics.

now_section.title: What I’m Currently Thinking About
now_section.lead: Questions and themes I’m actively using to steer reading, proof work, and modeling choices.

now_items: How to restore informative lower bounds under invariances: gauge-fixing vs. augmentation (e.g., augmented Lagrangian / ADMM-style structure).
How to make Isabelle proofs scale: interface design (locales), step-spec patterns, and reusable lemma libraries.
When a relaxation is “too loose”: minimal structural constraints that recover signal without breaking tractability.
How to evaluate discretization quality: objective proxies + constraint design for playability and interpretability.
How to keep research artifacts legible: short entry points + evidence links (notes/repos) without repeating the CV.
